key_insight: For the studied real-amplitude quantum generative circuits, the Fisher trace counts parameters rather than measuring fit, while kernel discrepancy adds no certification benefit in the reported shot-resolved tests.
engineering_relevance: Certification should test distributional accuracy directly and check whether combined metrics provide independent evidence rather than reflect circuit structure or benchmark construction.
method: Analyze Fisher information and amplitude-tree rank in noiseless statevector simulations.
Derive Wasserstein–discrepancy tolerance windows for two bitstring defect families.
Prove Hamming-cost redundancy bounds and an exponentially small worst-parity kernel minimax value.
evidence_signal: At experimentally resolvable tolerances, the numerical campaign found that the discrepancy vote changed no verdict at 1,000 shots or more.
watch_item: The false-pass guarantee does not extend to device noise, and pooled scores depend on optimizer convergence and scoring convention.
paper_title: Certifying quantum generative models beyond the Fisher trace
